lines.text: Cells, cells — more than organelles,
it's what they do that the SOL tells.
Membrane picks, ribosome builds,
mitochondria pay the bills.
Every part's got a job to do;
break a part, and the job breaks too.
Observe it first, then make a guess,
a hypothesis you can test.
Predict it: "if this, then that will show,"
then run it, and the data lets you know.
A law says what, it won't say why;
a theory explains, with proof piled high.
All living things are made of cells,
the smallest unit where life dwells,
and every cell comes from a cell.
Evidence? Yeast in a flask will tell:
it buds and clouds; the sealed flask stays clear —
no cell from nothing showed up here.
Then better lenses added more:
cells run metabolism at the core;
DNA gets passed from cell to cell,
and every cell's built the same as well.
Take the proof away, it's just a claim:
a hypothesis with a name.
Prokaryote: DNA loose inside,
no nucleus; flagella spin the ride.
Eukaryote: nucleus, organelles;
plants and animals, bigger cells.
Every cell has a membrane, DNA,
ribosomes, cytoplasm — four that stay.
Plants add a wall and chloroplasts for light;
one big vacuole keeps the stem upright.
Animals: no wall, small vacuoles,
and centrioles to help divide the whole.
Nucleus? No brain. It holds the plan,
the DNA — read it, build what you can.
Ribosomes build the protein chain;
rough ER folds it, sends it down the lane.
Golgi tags it, ships it from the cell —
production is something we can tell.
Mitochondria make the ATP;
lysosomes recycle the debris.
Block the Golgi: insulin can't leave;
it piles up; the blood has none to receive.
Unicellular: one cell, alone,
eats, moves, divides, all on its own.
Multicellular: they specialize;
cell, tissue, organ, system — watch them rise.
The organism's the top of the stack;
division of labor keeps each on track.
Interdependent: one part needs the rest;
the heart needs lungs; subsystems, that's the test.
Homeostasis: steady inside
while the outside world swings wide.
Heart rate: seventy, then you run —
one-fifty, pumping oxygen.
You rest; it settles back to seventy —
that's the balance, there for you to see.
Stomata open moist and cool,
close up hot and dry; that's the rule.
Roots dig deeper when the water's low;
the data on the graph is how you know.
Paramecium squeezes water out,
contractile vacuole: one cell, no doubt.
Lose the balance: swell, shrink, or shut down;
homeostasis broke — that's the breakdown.
Phospho-lipid: a phosphate head,
two lipid tails hang down instead.
Head's hydrophilic, loves the wet;
tails are hydrophobic — water's a threat.
Water's polar — oxygen pulls more;
heads face the water, tails hide in the core.
Draw it: two layers, heads out, tails in,
a bilayer, proteins floating within.
Integral proteins cross the wall —
a channel's a door straight through it all.
Peripheral sits on one side;
carbohydrate chains: ID tags outside.
Cholesterol wedged between the tails
keeps it fluid, so the wall never fails.
Selectively permeable — it picks,
so homeostasis holds and sticks.
If you're hydrophobic,
you've got vocabulary —
hydro's water, phobic's fear;
say the parts, and the word is clear.
Strip the proteins, and there's no door;
can't pick, can't pump — it's a bag, no more.
Semi-permeable: some get through.
Equilibrium: both sides even, too.
Passive transport: high to low,
no energy spent, just let it go.
Diffusion: down the gradient it goes;
bigger gap, faster — the table shows.
Facilitated: downhill, still free;
a protein carries it through, you see.
Osmosis: water crossing the wall;
water heads where the salt is, that's all.
Hypo- means under: less salt outside;
water rushes in, the cell swells wide.
Hyper- means over: more salt out there;
water leaves, the cell shrinks — beware.
Iso- means equal: in matches out;
the cell holds shape — that's what IV's about.
Salt a cucumber, it weeps on the plate;
seaweed in fresh water swells too great.
Active transport pumps it up the hill,
low to high, and ATP pays the bill.
Endo- means in: the membrane wraps it tight;
phagocytosis eats a bite,
pinocytosis drinks the tide;
exo- is out: a vesicle dumps outside.
That's how insulin leaves the cell;
the protein route ends there as well.
Cut the ATP: the pump stands still;
downhill keeps going; nothing climbs the hill.
Nucleus, ribosomes, rough ER, Golgi, lysosome, mitochondria, chloroplast, centrioles;
cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, flagella, organelles, prokaryotes, eukaryotes, homeostasis;
phospholipid bilayer, hydrophilic, hydrophobic, cholesterol, integral protein, peripheral protein, selectively permeable, diffusion;
passive transport, facilitated diffusion, osmosis, active transport, endocytosis, exocytosis, phagocytosis, pinocytosis.
Cells, cells — more than organelles.
You knew the parts; now know the job as well.
The fuel that drives more than a Humvee
and the enzyme that makes this rhyme —
that's Part 2, when Unit 3 comes.
